name: Brandweerkazerne Victor
description: A rationalist brick fire station on the Dapperstraat–Domselaerstraat corner, with twin arched fire-engine doors, paired corner gables and a small side balcony. Publieke Werken designed the 1911 building; the station opened in 1912.
funFact: Victor was Amsterdam’s first fire station without horse stables: its early electrically powered fire engines had a large charging station here. The V name dates from its former Pieter Vlamingstraat station. The original building combined fire station and living quarters; the whole building now serves the fire brigade.
